parameters.quote: Manufacturers must report every battery-related fire, thermal runaway, or other thermal incident involving injury, property damage, evacuation, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 5 calendar days of becoming aware of it. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported within 30 calendar days.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers must report every battery-related fire, thermal runaway, or other thermal incident involving injury, property damage, evacuation, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 5 calendar days of becoming aware of it. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported within 30 calendar days.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report every battery-related fire, thermal runaway, or other thermal incident involving injury, property damage, evacuation, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 5 calendar days of becoming aware of it. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported within 30 calendar days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 5 calendar days when an incident presents a material safety risk to their unit or requires customer action. Reports must include known circumstances and corrective actions; manufacturers must promptly update incomplete reports as facts are confirmed.

parameters.quote: Manufacturers must submit complete per-model results and test methods confidentially to the relevant regulator and provide complete per-model results, including failure-rate data, to customers considering or owning that model. A failure rate above 5% triggers regulator review, including consideration of test evidence, uncertainty, and the model's real-world safety record; the regulator may require additional testing, corrective action, or other proportionate safeguards.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Manufacturers must submit complete per-model results and test methods confidentially to the relevant regulator and provide complete per-model results, including failure-rate data, to customers considering or owning that model. A failure rate above 5% triggers regulator review, including consideration of test evidence, uncertainty, and the model's real-world safety record; the regulator may require additional testing, corrective action, or other proportionate safeguards.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and a representative sample, with testing repeated after material design changes. Manufacturers must submit complete per-model results and test methods confidentially to the relevant regulator and provide complete per-model results, including failure-rate data, to customers considering or owning that model. A failure rate above 5% triggers regulator review, including consideration of test evidence, uncertainty, and the model’s real-world safety record; the regulator may require additional testing, corrective action, or other proportionate safeguards. Regulators may publish aggregated or anonymized findings.

parameters.quote: Remote emergency shut-off is required for all newly manufactured home battery units beginning 24 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers must retrofit already-installed units to support remote emergency shut-off within 6 years after adoption, where technically feasible.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: Remote emergency shut-off is required for all newly manufactured home battery units beginning 24 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers must retrofit already-installed units to support remote emergency shut-off within 6 years after adoption, where technically feasible.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: Remote emergency shut-off is required for all newly manufactured home battery units beginning 24 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers must retrofit already-installed units to support remote emergency shut-off within 6 years after adoption, where technically feasible. Manufacturers must inform customers of units that cannot be retrofitted, explain available risk-reduction measures, and provide regulators with a remediation plan.

parameters.quote: All newly manufactured home battery units must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: All newly manufactured home battery units must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after adoption of this standard.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: All newly manufactured home battery units must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after adoption of this standard. The suppression system must be designed and validated for the unit’s battery chemistry and enclosure, and maintained in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions.

S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must provide customers clear safety notices promptly when a newly identified hazard may affect their unit, including the nature of the hazard, signs to watch for, and any actions to reduce risk. When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must promptly notify the relevant regulator and provide the supporting data and proposed corrective-action plan. The regulator must assess the evidence, including incident severity, trend, and effective corrective actions, and may require a recall or other proportionate safeguards. Manufacturers must notify affected customers without delay when a recall is ordered, explain the remedy and timeline, and provide progress updates until the remedy is completed.

judge_section_notes: The final S2 gives customers complete per-model failure-rate data and keeps regulator submissions confidential, but sets no permanent limit and no sales stop, so a 5% failure rate only triggers review. S5 turns the 8-per-100k threshold into a notification and review trigger rather than a mandatory recall, leaving recall to regulator discretion. S3's six-year retrofit period and S4's 36-month suppression deadline sit inside the acceptable ranges.
